title: Director, Technology Audit
description:
About this role Your team Internal Audit’s mission is to provide independent assurance to the Board of Directors and Executive Management that BlackRock’s businesses are effectively managed and achieving strategic, operational, and risk management objectives. The Technology Audit team is a global function operating across the United States, Europe, and Asia, partnering with technology and business leaders to assess risk, evaluate control effectiveness, and provide insights that strengthen governance, resilience, and operational performance. The team delivers assurance across application platforms, infrastructure environments, information security, data management, and technology-enabled business processes, helping build confidence that BlackRock meets its commitments to clients, shareholders, employees, and other stakeholders. Your role and impact As a Technology Audit Director, you will lead risk-based assurance activities across BlackRock’s technology landscape while serving as a trusted advisor to senior technology executives and business stakeholders. You will oversee the execution of the annual audit plan, drive enterprise-wide risk assessments, and provide leadership across complex technology and data-related audits. This role requires strong stakeholder management, strategic thinking, and deep technology expertise to influence control environments and support business objectives. In addition, you will play a key leadership role in advancing the global technology audit function through innovation, continuous improvement, and talent development. Your responsibilities In every role at BlackRock, you'll be expected to apply sound judgement and critical thinking to solve complex problems, adapt as the business evolves, and combine the curiosity to explore new approaches and technologies with the rigor to challenge the results. The scope of this role also includes the following responsibilities: Provide leadership and oversight as the Accountable Audit Director and Independent Audit Director for assurance reviews evaluating the controls supporting the design, development, implementation, and operation of technology solutions across the firm. Serve as the primary relationship manager for senior technology stakeholders, developing a deep understanding of business strategies, operating models, key initiatives, and emerging risks. Build and maintain strong partnerships with technology leadership, Information Security, Technology Risk Management, and other control functions to promote effective risk management and coordinated assurance activities. Oversee risk assessments and the delivery of the annual audit plan across core technology, data, infrastructure, and technology-enabled business functions. Lead, coach, and develop a team of audit professionals by providing meaningful feedback, mentorship, and growth opportunities while fostering a high-performance culture. Manage resources effectively to optimize productivity, support talent development, and deliver high-quality assurance and advisory engagements. Champion process improvements that enhance efficiency, accountability, consistency, and the overall effectiveness of the audit function. Your experience Bachelor’s degree required; undergraduate or graduate degree in management information systems, engineering, computer science, or a related technology discipline preferred. Strong understanding of technology architecture, processes, risks, controls, frameworks (CoBIT, MITRE ATT&CK, ISO, ITIL and COSO), and industry standards across, cloud environments, infrastructure, artificial intelligence, information security, data management and applications.. Direct experience in technology audit, technology risk, or a related control function within a complex organization, preferably in financial services. Proven ability to lead, develop, and retain teams of highly skilled professionals while fostering a collaborative and inclusive environment. Strong project management, organizational, and presentation skills, with the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment. Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, including experience preparing audit reports, executive presentations, and stakeholder communications. Demonstrated ability to build credibility and maintain effective relationships with executive management, regulators, and cross-functional partners. 
For New York, NY Only the salary range for this position is USD$194,000.00 - USD$270,000.00 . Additionally, employees are eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, and benefits including healthcare, leave benefits, and retirement benefits. BlackRock operates a pay-for-performance compensation philosophy and your total compensation may vary based on role, location, and firm, department and individual performance.

title: Senior GBS Financial Operations Manager
description: CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at  www.coreweave.com . About the Team The Global Business Services function is a new and critical team designed to centralize and standardize CoreWeave's foundational business processes across Finance, HR, and Procurement. We are a results-oriented, highly collaborative, and technically minded team reporting to the Head of Global Business Services, with a mandate to drive transformation and operational maturity as CoreWeave scales globally and matures as a public company. Key Responsibilities: The Senior GBS Financial Operations Manager will lead our GBS function, driving efficiency and excellence across our core business processes. You will be responsible for defining and optimizing global end-to-end business processes, ensuring compliance, and delivering measurable improvements in efficiency and service quality across our worldwide operations. This involves leading a global team, championing process automation, and acting as a key partner to executive stakeholders to support CoreWeave's hyper-growth. You will be directly responsible for establishing robust controls and metrics-driven service delivery for critical back-office functions. Process Excellence & Standardization: Define, map, and implement global, standardized, and best-in-class end-to-end processes for Procure-to-Pay (P2P), Hire-to-Retire (HR), Order-to-Cash (OTC) and Record-to-Report (R2R). Drive continuous process improvement initiatives leveraging lean methodologies to enhance efficiency and reduce costs. Performance Management & Reporting: Define, track, and report on Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for all GBS functions. You will be strong on reporting and actioning on KPIs, using data analytics to identify bottlenecks, drive continuous improvement, and measure service delivery effectiveness across the globe. Operational Management: Partner with each of the GBS shared services functions, ensuring timely and accurate execution of tasks related to managing departmental budgets and invoices, vendor management, training and financial closing procedures. Compliance & Governance: Establish robust internal controls and processes to ensure GBS complies with SOX 404 requirements. You'll manage operational risk, third-party providers, and ensure business continuity for GBS operations. AI Enablement & Agentic Operations: Identify, pilot, and scale AI tooling across our processes to automate manual accounting and shared services. You will build the operating model for responsible AI adoption, including use case prioritization, human-in-the-loop review, data governance, and change management, while upskilling the team to design and maintain their own AI-enabled workflows.  Technology & Digital Transformation: Champion the implementation and optimization of GBS technology platforms (e.g., ERP, workflow automation tools like RPA) to maximize efficiency, data quality, and scalability. Stakeholder Partnership & Communication: Utilize excellent communication and partnership skills to act as a key strategic partner to global functional leaders (Finance, HR, Procurement) to manage SLAs and align GBS strategy with CoreWeave's objectives. Project & Change Management: Own and drive large-scale, cross-functional projects, such as system implementations (e.g., ERP upgrades, HRIS rollouts), M&A integrations to the GBS processes, or process re-engineering efforts. Demonstrate strong project management skills to deliver projects on time and within budget. Qualifications:  8+ years of progressive experience in Finance, Operations, or Shared Services, with at least 3 years in a management role leading a Global Business Services or Shared Services organization. Experience working in a publicly traded company environment, with a strong, practical understanding of SOX 404 compliance, internal controls, and financial reporting requirements. Demonstrable track record of scaling global shared service centers, including experience managing teams across different geographies and time zones. Deep expertise in business process analysis, design, and implementation, specifically related to procure-to-pay, record-to-report, and Hire-to-Retire. Proven ability to manage significant departmental budgets and invoicing processes, with an eye toward cost optimization and control. title: HMDA/Fair Lending Manager
description: About Upstart At Upstart, we’re united by a mission that matters: to radically reduce the cost and complexity of borrowing for all Americans. Every day, we bring creativity, experimentation, and advanced AI to reshape access to credit, helping millions move forward financially with clarity and confidence. As the leading AI lending marketplace, we partner with banks and credit unions to expand access to affordable credit through technology that’s both radically intelligent and deeply human. Our platform runs over one million predictions per borrower using more than 3,000 signals, powering smarter, fairer decisions for millions of customers. But the numbers only hint at the impact. Every idea, every voice, and every contribution moves us closer to a world where credit never stands between people and their financial progress. We’re proudly digital-first, giving most Upstarters the flexibility to do their best work from wherever they thrive, alongside teammates across 80+ cities in the US and Canada. Digital-first doesn’t mean distant. We’re intentional about in-person connection through team onsites, planning sessions, and moments that spark creativity and trust. And whether you choose to work primarily from home or collaborate in-person from one of our offices in Columbus, Austin, the Bay Area, or New York City, you’ll have the support to work in the way that works best for you. If you’re energized by tackling meaningful problems, excited to innovate with purpose, and motivated by work that truly matters, we’d love to hear from you. The Team:  Upstart’s Responsible AI Lending team supports fair and responsible lending practices through compliance oversight, analysis, and controls. The team partners across Product Compliance, Fair Lending, and Model Risk to identify and manage regulatory risk while supporting Upstart Bank’s continued growth. As the HMDA / Fair Lending Manager , you will own key elements of Upstart Bank’s Home Mortgage Disclosure Act compliance program, with a focus on data integrity, reporting, and second-line oversight. You will establish and manage the HMDA quality program while expanding your impact over time through geographic analysis, Fair Lending support, and thoughtful use of automation to make compliance reviews more effective and scalable. How you’ll make an impact Own the HMDA data-quality lifecycle, including periodic Loan/Application Register reviews, quarterly and annual filing preparation, and oversight of reporting accuracy and timeliness. Identify data-quality issues and root causes, partner with business teams on corrective actions, and monitor remediation through resolution. Build and maintain a risk-based HMDA sampling and quality-assurance program that provides an effective second-line challenge of business-owned reporting data. Perform and support geographic analysis of lending patterns to identify potential redlining and other Fair Lending risks and contribute to broader Fair Lending monitoring. Partner with Product Compliance, Fair Lending, Model Risk, and business teams to clarify responsibilities, improve controls, and promote consistent data-quality practices. Use automation and Generative AI responsibly to improve sampling, anomaly detection, trend analysis, and documentation while maintaining appropriate human review for regulatory interpretation and reporting decisions. Minimum Qualifications  4+ years of hands-on experience reviewing HMDA Loan/Application Register data and applying HMDA data integrity, geocoding, and reporting requirements. Experience preparing, reviewing, or supporting quarterly and annual HMDA submissions in a regulated lending or financial-services environment. Experience performing root-cause analysis of compliance or regulatory data issues and coordinating remediation with business or operational teams. Working knowledge of applicable Fair Lending requirements, including the Equal Credit Opportunity Act/Regulation B and Fair Housing Act. Experience performing compliance testing, quality assurance, monitoring, or other second-line oversight activities involving regulated lending data.   Preferred Qualifications Knowledge of geographic or redlining analysis used to support Fair Lending monitoring. Experience building or improving risk-based sampling methodologies, quality-control programs, or compliance monitoring frameworks. Ability to work across compliance, product, model risk, and business teams to resolve data-quality and regulatory issues. Experience using scripting, analytics, automation, or Generative AI tools to improve regulatory data review and identify anomalous patterns.
